AfterCardPlayed.issue: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04: the sim's own architecture for the Wither's upgrade-matching CHANGED since the last audit and the record's mechanism description is stale on that one point, though the verdict and both named dormant gaps still hold. The mechanism is right -- count the target player's card plays down from 6, add a Wither to HAND at 0, reset to 6. What changed: the upgrade matching is NO LONGER open-coded inline in `on_card_played` (the old text's `for _ in range(wither_upgrade_count): wither.fake_upgrade()` no longer exists there); it now runs through a shared listener, `Aeonglass.on_card_generated_for_combat` (monsters/glory/aeonglass.py:44-64), fired by `CardPileCmd.add_to_hand`'s `AfterCardGeneratedForCombat` dispatch, which the class's own comment (aeonglass.py:49) says now maps directly to `Aeonglass.cs`'s `MatchWitherToUpgradeCount` (Aeonglass.cs:160-166) -- catching a Wither from ANY source (the boss's own Increasing Intensity Wither AND this power's punish Wither) through one hook, same shape as the real game, rather than two open-coded sites. This is a FIDELITY IMPROVEMENT over the text it replaces, not a regression, and does not change either of the two findings below, which are about the COUNTER, not the upgrade-matching. Two findings, unchanged. (1) The COUNTER'S IDENTITY is conflated: C# keeps `CardsLeft` as a DynamicVar whose canonical default is 6 (WitheringPresencePower.cs:16,28) and resets it to the LITERAL `6m` (:57), entirely independent of `base.Amount`; the sim initialises and resets `_cards_left` from `self.amount` (powers.py:4126, 4136). Those coincide only because both appliers pass 6 -- Aeonglass.cs:82 applies `6m` and monsters/glory/aeonglass.py:20,41 applies `_WITHERING_PRESENCE = 6` -- so a Withering Presence applied at any other amount, or STACKED (StackType is Counter, so stacking really does raise Amount), would reset to the wrong number in the sim and to 6 in the game. DORMANT, by enumeration of the two appliers. (2) hook_dispatch gap G4: the sim fires on_card_played once per play where C# fires AfterCardPlayed once per CardPlay iteration, so a Throwing-Axe- or One-Two-Punch-doubled card advances the counter by 1 in the sim and by 2 in the game -- G4 is already LIVE with an executed witness and is not re-verdicted; the per-unit consequence is that Wither arrives later in the sim. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Citations renumbered 2026-08-04.
